scenarios.actor: Digital Agency as selector, purchaser and platform operator; ministry system owners; suppliers. AISI participation would need agreement, not an assumed veto.
scenarios.lever: New FY2027 selection and separate paid procurement. Require priced, published evidence and lifecycle terms in a lawful new tender. No located right to change existing vendor contracts unilaterally.
scenarios.safeguard: Proposed marginal addition: identify the deployed model/tool version; retain reproducible deployment-level leakage tests; material changes trigger review; defined incidents trigger evidence preservation, reporting and proportionate suspension/cure where expressly contracted.
scenarios.politicalEconomicEvidence: Existing trial requires benchmark evidence and explanation of hallucination, bias and harmful-content controls; FY2027 plan already seeks safety explanations and tool-use details. May announcement reports 15 applications and five contracted companies, with paid procurement planned. Government wants domestic AI capability and stable demand. None of this establishes assent to new duties, a contract value, vendor revenue dependence or foreign-frontier leverage. Direct NEC page fetch returned 403; no company-specific acceptance claim is relied on.

roleStressTest.role: Purchaser and vendor, separately labelled assumptions
roleStressTest.objection: Purchaser assumption: delaying an April rollout or losing useful domestic models undermines adoption. Vendor assumption: open-ended tests, public vulnerability details and uncontrolled retests increase cost and expose IP.
roleStressTest.response: Proposed: publish a bounded acceptance suite and material-change definition before bids; price retests; separate confidential evidence from public summary; maintain a tested fallback model/workflow. Measure user migration, latency, remediation cost and rejected bidders rather than assume bargaining power.
roleStressTest.evidenceVsAssumption: Demand policy and five signed trial participants are reported by the government (jp-next); objections, willingness to accept amended clauses, fallback adequacy and costs are untested assumptions. Survey records competing AI use, but not whether it is an authorised contractual substitute.

scenarios.selectionGate: By proposed November 30, 2026 check: obtain actual new call, authorised tender owner and route for incorporating terms before bids. Advance only if a bounded clause can be adopted lawfully without claiming already-required safety evidence as additional. If final tender disallows the addition, test voluntary acceptance separately and label it accordingly.
scenarios.pilotDesign: Proposed April–May 2027: shadow-run the deployed agent with synthetic secrets and permission-separated tools. Compare existing selection-only baseline with versioned test/containment process on identical held-out tasks; include model-change and incident drills. Randomise task order, blind human adjudication, record all attempts, and never expose live secrets merely to demonstrate a failure.

successMeasure.observedAdoptionProxy: (1698 + 711 + 669) / 6439 = 3078 / 6439, approximately 0.4780, use at least weekly among survey respondents. Not national adoption or safeguard coverage.
successMeasure.proposedOperationalCoverage: Versioned deployments with signed obligations and complete evidence / all eligible deployments in the frozen purchaser inventory; also transaction-weighted coverage. Values unknown until inventory and contracts exist.
successMeasure.proposedMarginalEffect: Leak-free completed tasks / all attempted held-out tasks, with correctness and leakage also separate; compare intervention and baseline, report raw counts and uncertainty. Delay, cost and lawful fallback-use outcomes are co-primary. No catastrophic-risk fraction inferred.

scenarios.baselineNeeded: Full FY2026 executed terms and FY2027 tender; existing incident/version clauses; workflow inventory; current safeguards; task distribution, usage logs and supplier prices. Survey cannot replace logs or identify purchases reached by the proposed clauses.
scenarios.whatCouldBeValidatedByGeneva: Conditionally: actual clause adoption and signed supply, model/version traceability, ability to halt a deliberately failing shadow deployment, incident-drill timeliness, and held-out leakage improvement in a bounded workflow.
scenarios.whatCannot: National or global model-release control; reduction of rare catastrophic incidents; FY2027 full-year performance; contractual addition before seeing the final tender; applicability to all 180,000 intended users.
scenarios.stopRule: Reject route-as-procurement if no authorised published clause or supplier acceptance. Reject efficacy claim if baseline already provides the same control, tasks are contaminated, or failure reduction disappears after accounting for task completion/fallback migration.

scenarios.actor: One named Singapore deploying organisation and its authorised system/procurement owner; its agent supplier and selected technical tester. IMDA/AIVF run the sandbox; SG/KR AISI methods are optional inputs.
scenarios.lever: Voluntary commercial testing agreement plus the purchaser's own signed go/no-go acceptance condition. This is a narrower, testable alternative to an unverified government-wide AISI deployment mandate.
scenarios.safeguard: Proposed: testing must change an actual release or permission decision. Gate external sending and access to sensitive data on held-out leakage and prompt-injection results; require remediation/retest and review of material updates, with a human-only fallback.
scenarios.politicalEconomicEvidence: The ongoing sandbox advertises commercial tester choice, some funding, production or intended-production applications and three-month testing/case-study completion; it lists 30 applications across 12 geographies and 14 industries, with no global eligible-app denominator. Joint Earlybird/Knovel materials document accounting-agent tests on approximately 100 documents and report Earlybird spent 3 days and Knovel contributed 25 days; currency cost and staffing units are unspecified. October ministerial answer favours collaboration and does not mandate frontier-model access. Fit of a voluntary application-level purchasing gate is an inference, not approval.

roleStressTest.role: Purchaser and vendor/tester, separately labelled assumptions
roleStressTest.objection: Purchaser assumption: a voluntary report that cannot stop release adds expense without changed behaviour. Vendor/tester assumption: buyer-specific pass bars and public case-study requirements create liability, disclosure costs and false assurance.
roleStressTest.response: Proposed: get the deployment owner's signature before testing; make criteria task-specific and human-validated; contract disclosure boundaries compatible with programme publication; price a single bounded remediation cycle; permit different tester or non-agent workflow after failure.
roleStressTest.evidenceVsAssumption: Rolling participation, commercial partner choice and publication are observed (sg-sandbox). Commercial willingness, exact delegated signatory, funding award, reproducibility and acceptance of contractual remedies are unknown. Company-authored case study is participation evidence, not independent causal proof.

scenarios.selectionGate: By proposed January 31, 2027: obtain purchaser delegation, live-workflow inventory, tester/vendor agreement, admission if using the sandbox, and permission to report a bounded result. Without an empowered purchaser, retain only a methods experiment and do not call it a deployment gate.
scenarios.pilotDesign: Proposed February–April three-month test, May independent retest. Use a consenting document-processing agent with read and send permissions separated. Reproduce baseline workflow, inject synthetic sensitive records and malicious instructions, then apply permission limits and a signed release gate. Use unseen documents and memory-reset versus persistent-memory runs; adjudicate correctness and leakage independently. Port a subset to a KR or JP evaluator only as an optional reproducibility test, never as presumed recognition.

successMeasure.proposedCoverage: Production/intended-production applications with empowered signed gate / all eligible applications in that purchaser's frozen inventory. Also report affected transaction share; values unknown.
successMeasure.proposedBehaviour: Failed candidate versions actually withheld or remediated / all versions failing pre-specified criteria; report undefined, not zero, if none fail.
successMeasure.proposedMarginalEffect: Leak-free correctly completed held-out tasks / all attempted tasks in each arm, plus separate correctness, leakage and fallback-use counts. Cross-lab agreement = identical accept/reject decisions / paired evaluated cases, not a recognition score.
successMeasure.observedProgrammeSize: 30 applications is a programme reach count, not 30 successful safeguards and not the eligible Singapore economy.

scenarios.whatCouldBeValidatedByGeneva: Selection and consent; an actual withheld release or removed permission; repeatable leakage reduction in a bounded workflow; measured compliance effort; a completed case study subject to consent and publication timing.
scenarios.whatCannot: A national mandatory gate, universal frontier-model access, regional mutual recognition, independent proof of the participant case study's broad safety, or a national adoption rate.
scenarios.stopRule: Stop gate claim if purchaser cannot refuse deployment, parties cannot agree publication/terms, or only test accuracy improves with no actual deployment consequence. Do not delay conclusion waiting indefinitely for voluntary recruitment.

scenarios.lever: Readiness and operationalisation of safety duties after checking the operative text and system applicability. February draft is a concrete design lead, not treated as binding current law.
scenarios.safeguard: Proposed incremental control: executable incident escalation, material-change evidence refresh and independent reproduction of a risk-mitigation test, rather than a merely written safety case.
scenarios.politicalEconomicEvidence: MSIT's January commencement release prioritises industry development/minimum regulation, announces at least one year's enforcement grace and confidential/anonymous support consultations, and envisages guideline refinement. Retrieved February notice concerns lifecycle risk controls and submission/reporting; its comment deadline was February 26, 2026. Draft external verification of compute data requires business consent. No current revision, final promulgated notice, enforcement start or participating firm's consent is established.

roleStressTest.role: Purchaser of evaluation/compliance owner and AI vendor, separately labelled assumptions
roleStressTest.objection: Compliance-owner assumption: spending on a draft or an out-of-scope system has little value; simulated compliance may be mistaken for legal approval. Developer assumption: revealing compute or sensitive model information to another institute exposes secrets and may exceed actual duties.
roleStressTest.response: First verify current legal instrument and applicability. Use confidential evidence, a scoped voluntary drill and no certification claim; offer executable evidence of mitigation without requiring public model secrets. Separate statutory reporting from voluntarily purchased evaluation.
roleStressTest.evidenceVsAssumption: Industry-development emphasis, grace and confidential support are official statements (kr-commencement); consent language is in a draft (kr-draft). Incentives, budgets, operating receipt channel and willingness to participate are not observed.

scenarios.selectionGate: Do not select as a legislative-window route. Before a proposed February pilot, retrieve promulgated notice and latest enforcement position, identify in-scope obligor and recipient, then obtain a consenting developer. Otherwise retain as rejected/unknown legislative lead and optional research-only tabletop.
scenarios.pilotDesign: February–April proposed tabletop with synthetic incident and model-change events. Rehearse detection, triage, evidence preservation and submission readiness; independently replay one mitigation test. If operative law matches the draft, use its deadlines; otherwise adapt the test to the current text. Never send a false incident to authorities.

successMeasure.proposedCoverage: In-scope model versions with verified current safety-case evidence / all in-scope model versions held by participating developer. Both counts unknown.
successMeasure.proposedReadiness: Drill events with complete correctly routed evidence within applicable deadline / all assigned drill events; raw counts and evaluator agreement required.
successMeasure.proposedMarginalEffect: Compare baseline written policy with rehearsed workflow on matched unseen events; measure incomplete/missed escalations and successful mitigation retests. This is simulated operational performance, not observed legal compliance or risk reduction.

scenarios.baselineNeeded: Final notice and amendments; current enforcement grace; system eligibility; authorised submission channel; existing incident process; developer inventory and evaluation budget. January press release's FLOP threshold description is not a complete applicability opinion.
scenarios.whatCouldBeValidatedByGeneva: Whether a real legal/purchaser path exists; if parties consent, completeness and timeliness of a drill and reproducibility of one risk mitigation. An evidence-backed decision not to select the route also meets the selection objective.
scenarios.whatCannot: An open January 2027 drafting window, universal Korean AI coverage, a confirmed end to enforcement grace, adoption of draft deadlines as law, or real incident-risk reduction from a tabletop.
scenarios.stopRule: Stop legislative claim immediately absent a live official revision. Stop statutory compliance claim if operative text/applicability cannot be established. No consenting obligor by proposed January 31 means no promised pre-Geneva operational validation.

Korean final promulgated notice, later amendments, latest grace-period decision and 2027 consultation calendar remain unknown. February draft deadlines must never be represented as current law. Search absence is not legal absence.

Gen-nai survey numerator/denominator measure use within a voluntary respondent sample, not regulatory reach or safeguard adoption. Unregistered respondents are included in the denominator. Do not divide respondents by the approximate 180,000 target to claim a response rate without a matching sampling frame.
Singapore programme's 30 applications is international and cumulative/undated on its page; no successful-gate numerator, Singapore-specific denominator, or market-wide rate is established.

No sourced GDP or supply-chain share is used in this route comparison. Such fractions would describe economic exposure, not jurisdictional control or causal safety impact. Do not reuse ordinal ratings or convert them to 0–1.
